---
title: "F200 Space Exploration worker-speed tail-ten fixture"
---

This disposable fixture is a reduced Factorio 2.0.77 / Space Exploration 0.7.57 worker-speed tail-ten boundary. It is not Gamer433's save, does not reproduce mining or ore effects, and does not claim physical science production. The original worker-six fixture commit and its adverse controls remain in the merged fixture history; this r02 actor instead pins the observed named `worker-robots-speed-10` tail.

The original actor has three explicit wrappers sharing one narrow common fixture actor. `source/` is `0.4.0`, uses published MIR `5.0.20015` with cap zero, and creates only the protected source state. `cap10/` is `0.5.0`, uses the same published MIR package with cap ten, records the expected adverse public frame, and then stops with `MIR_EXPECTED_OLD15_CAP_NOT_ENFORCED`. `successor16/` is `0.6.0`, uses candidate MIR `5.0.20016` with cap ten, and is the only original role that may create the custom lab, observe one ordinary completion, save, or cold-read.

The separate current-state reset-event roles retain those original wrappers unchanged. `current-old15/` is `0.7.0` with published MIR `5.0.20015`; `current-successor16/` is `0.8.0` with candidate MIR `5.0.20016`. They use the controller-bound A0 save only as a base input, never read its old fixture storage or treat its original scripted facts as valid continuation preconditions. After recording all three existing public named forces (`player`, `mir5-worker-speed-cap-ten-foreign`, and `mir5-worker-speed-cap-ten-earned`) after provider normalization, they construct one declared synthetic public boundary through whole `research_queue` assignment: player current level ten at 27% with two target occurrences, enabled foreign level eleven with automation at 42%, and enabled earned level thirteen idle work. The provider observation records the `stone-wall` sentinel without imposing a pre-admin value; the declared baseline requires it disabled and records it on every force thereafter. The named worker-nine/deep-one prerequisites and the foreign automation/electricity prerequisites are explicit. No new force, broad enabling, recursive research, private MIR storage, lifecycle/caps call, remote call, or raised event is used.

Each current-state role records the declared administrative intent, wrapped public pre-reset frames, exactly three ordered `reset_technology_effects` calls, every observed reset event, and per-force frames returned from each call. The actor does not claim an exclusive MIR event writer. Published15 exports that complete reset observation and then stops with `MIR_EXPECTED_CURRENT_OLD15_RESET_NOT_ENFORCED`, without a lab or save. Candidate16 requires only the current target queue to reduce to one retained level-ten occurrence at 27%, foreign and earned over-cap targets to disable while the automation sentinel remains current, and the unrelated sentinel to remain unchanged. It observes post-reset bonus rather than assuming an absolute baseline; one ordinary level-ten completion must add the literal `0.65` effect to that observation.

`current-observe16` is a separate `0.9.0` private-candidate (`5.0.20016`) mechanism observer. It retains the exact current-state administrative write order—prerequisites for all three named forces, then player tuple/queue/progress, foreign tuple/queue/progress, then earned tuple/empty queue—and records public three-force frames before administration, after every declared write boundary, after administration and after one passive tick. Its one final `current-observe.json` trace has one shared sequence across frames and observed public research/effects-reset events; event rows name their boundary and available force/research/by-script fields but never infer an internal writer. It retains the current-successor16 fixture-lab prototype in the data stage but never creates, feeds, or researches with that lab at runtime, and stops with `MIR_EXPECTED_CURRENT_OBSERVE16_TRACE_COMPLETE` before any explicit reset, runtime lab, save or cold action. This is neither an r06 retry nor a qualification of public16, current17, an upgrade, or the reporter case.

Candidate current-state completion uses the same bounded eight-pack lab refills and two-tick active hold as the original actor, then saves once as `mir5-worker-speed-cap-current-state-complete` and reads that same completed save twice cold. Its `current-{provider,pre-reset,post-reset,pre-work,complete,cold}.json` records retain the full reset trace, pre-work and post-completion accounting; cold reads never redo synthetic setup or resets. This is reduced synthetic current-state reset-event coverage only. It does not qualify a save upgrade, Space Exploration configuration, whole-force bonus preservation, prior foreign-disabled ownership, the original reporter case, physical full-cost science, GUI/client/performance work, or stable delivery.

The observed target contract is deliberately literal: tail ten is infinite with one `worker-robot-speed` effect of `0.65`; its direct prerequisites are `worker-robots-speed-9` and `se-deep-space-science-pack-1`; its unit formula is `0.2*(2^(L-6)*1000)` at 60 seconds; and each of eight ingredients has amount one: automation, logistic, chemical, utility, space, SE rocket, SE energy four, and SE deep-space one. Data-final guards that contract and only creates a fixture lab with exactly those named inputs. It does not edit the target technology's prototypes, costs, effects, or ingredients.

Source setup is scripted and labelled. It records tail ten at level ten with 27% retained current work and two queued occurrences; it records a foreign level-eleven disabled force with its automation queue at 42%; and it records a separate level-thirteen earned force. It explicitly marks the two direct worker prerequisites on all three actor forces and, for the foreign automation sentinel only, automation science plus its observed direct `electricity` prerequisite. It never calls broad prototype enablement and preserves every unrelated technology flag. Named setup callbacks are labelled administrative only for these three forces; no scripted callback can count as ordinary tail-ten completion.

The published-15 adverse wrapper writes `script-output/worker-speed-cap-ten/old-negative.json` and emits `[MIR_WORKER_SPEED_CAP_TEN phase=old-negative]` before its expected stop. That body contains public player, foreign, and earned force frames, source and active MIR tuple fields, exact mods, queue/progress, bonuses, and an absent lab. It proves the expected old outcome through public state: player tail ten remains enabled with two occurrences and 27% current progress; the foreign sentinel remains disabled with automation at 42%; and the earned level-thirteen force remains enabled and idle. It makes no assertion about another mod's private storage.

The successor wrapper receives that same protected source state only after the player's runtime has reconciled the cap. It emits `pre-work.json` before creating or feeding the fixture lab, then allows one real ordinary, non-scripted level-ten completion. The lab has a void energy source and uses bounded accepted-count refills; it neither assigns energy nor assumes the full unit count fits inventory. Snapshots expose every actual input count and cumulative scripted feed. After completion the lab remains active for two ticks; the state requires no level-eleven start, no queued level-eleven retry, unchanged public foreign and earned frames, and unchanged per-pack input/feed values across the hold. It saves only then, as `mir5-worker-speed-cap-ten-complete`.

Every marker serializes its single JSON body to `script-output/worker-speed-cap-ten/{source,old-negative,pre-work,complete,cold}.json` and logs that body under `[MIR_WORKER_SPEED_CAP_TEN phase=...]`. Bodies include the exact active mods tuple/count, fixture and MIR versions, cap, formula/time labels, target effect, full three-force snapshots, ordinary event rows, setup/admin labels, queue attempt result, and lab accounting. Cold `on_load` only sets local flags; its following one-tick read validates and writes a cold observation without mutating world or fixture storage. A governed controller must bind exact archives and independently review any native output; fixture and host controls alone are not native qualification.
